Why is AI always viewed through the lens of our current economic system? Why not see the economic system itself as something malleable, rather than an unchangeable force like the sky or earth? Our economy is man-made, it can be reformed or entirely replaced to better serve humanity’s true interests instead of being bound by warped materialistic beliefs. AI is just a tool; the real issue is how we choose to structure society. Instead of fearing AI because of the flaws in our current system, we should be rethinking the system itself to ensure it serves our needs while respecting resources and natural laws.

The solution is Open Direct Competent Democracy (ODCD) and the Natural Law Economy (NLE). ODCD removes corrupt leadership by letting the public make decisions with expert guidance, ensuring policies are based on competence, not greed. NLE replaces artificial financial constraints with a resource-based system that prioritizes human well-being, sustainability, and efficient use of resources without harming nature. Instead of adapting to a broken system, we should build one that truly benefits humanity.

LLM's are riffing by picking up key words or styles of each question posed by the users, then formulating a response from the wealth of information available within your data base, so they can predict which words to apply in their answers, thus riffing an understanding. In reality, they're just mimicking. I've tested this with LLM's and they frequently get their answers wrong or incomplete, if they fail to pull from a wide range of sources. 
Well if LLM's can make error, then LQM's can do the same when it comes to predicting sequences to solve health or science problems. The problem is, the pure number of sequences AI can test, far exceed what humans can do. If any part of the data is wrong or isn't being sought by AI, the answers may look correct, but the human may not fully understand what they're looking at and act on this flawed AI conclusion.
AI may not be the solution everyone thinks it is. After all they are just tools and not thinking entities.
